faqs.question: Do we need a developer?
faqs.answer: The direct connection flows guide you through Shopify or WooCommerce. A supported product feed can start an import. Checkout and theme configuration may need your store team.

faqs.question: Will it change our brand voice?
faqs.answer: Rewrites start from existing facts. Apply generates and publishes a listing rewrite; structured data has a separate control. There is no generated-copy preview before Apply today.

faqs.question: We also sell through retailers and Amazon. Does this help there?

faqs.question: How long until something changes?

sections.title: Three ways to start.

items.title: Audit
items.body: 4 weeks, fixed fee. A baseline of how assistants answer agreed questions in one category, the data issues worth investigating and a prioritized fix list for your team.

items.title: Pilot
items.body: 6 weeks, one market, one category. Baseline at week 0, agreed data changes and the same questions at week 6. Any outcome-linked fee and target are agreed in advance.

items.title: Design study
items.body: 3 months, with scopes that can run up to 6. For checkout or booking questions that need more than a fix list. The scope can include a prototype with dummy data and agreed readouts.

sections.note: Fees depend on scope and are agreed on the first call. These are service engagements; the pilot readout follows the method agreed with your team.

items.title: Week 0: baseline
items.body: We agree the questions at kickoff and run each one several times on every assistant, before changing data.

items.title: Weeks 1 to 5: fix
items.body: Work on the agreed category and test checkout where it applies. Public-data work is handed to your team; direct changes need explicit authorization.

items.title: Week 6 · Re-run
items.body: Repeat the agreed questions with the same assistants and number of runs. Document model or access changes.

items.title: Readout
items.body: Review what moved, the limits of the method and proposed next steps. You decide whether to continue.

sections.title: What we measure.

items.title: Named
items.body: How often an answer includes your product.

items.title: Position
items.body: Where the product appears among the options in the sampled answer.

items.title: Linked
items.body: Whether an answer links the shopper to your store.

items.title: Bought
items.body: Whether the agreed test flow can complete an order or needs a payment handoff.

sections.note: We can also record wrong prices, stock or specifications in the sampled answers. Targets and collection methods are agreed in writing; these measures are not all automated dashboard features.

meta.title: Selling wine and spirits through AI assistants
meta.description: See the bottle facts assistants can compare: strength, age, region, style, size and availability. Prepare your data within platform restrictions.

wine-and-spirits.title: Selling wine and spirits when AI picks the bottle.
wine-and-spirits.description: Ask an assistant for a gift bottle and strength, age, origin and price matter. Make those facts available as text and product data, while respecting the age and regional restrictions of each sales channel.
questions: Smoky single malt under $80 for a gift
A Barolo that is ready to drink now
Low-sugar rum for cocktails

faqs.question: Can AI buy alcohol for a shopper?
faqs.answer: It depends on the channel, location and age-verification flow. ecentic does not grant permission to sell a restricted product or guarantee a compliant automated purchase.

faqs.question: Do we need a GTIN on every bottle?
faqs.answer: Use the correct manufacturer-assigned identifier where one exists. Do not invent a GTIN for a limited release or reuse another product’s identifier.

faqs.question: What about limited releases with no stock feed?
faqs.answer: Keep the public listing and any supported import accurate. The importer does not create a live inventory connector for an unsupported platform.

faqs.question: How do age checks work with agent checkout?
faqs.answer: Validate your store’s exact requirements on a staging flow. The current checkout implementation does not establish a universal alcohol age-verification solution.

faqs.question: Does this work for thousands of bottles?
faqs.answer: Start with a supported catalog import and one category. Self-serve plan limits stay in place; larger scopes are agreed for an enterprise pilot.

faqs.question: Will AI repeat our health claims?
faqs.answer: An assistant may use published statements. Keep them accurate and permitted in your market. Rewrites start from source product facts; they do not validate a health claim.

faqs.question: Does nutrition data need to be text as well as a label photo?
faqs.answer: Providing it as readable text gives tools an explicit source to inspect. An image alone does not supply the same structured fields.

faqs.question: We sell through supermarkets. Does this help?
faqs.answer: It helps you work on your own store and supported data sources. A retailer controls its own listings; ecentic does not rewrite them through your account.

faqs.question: How should multipacks appear?
faqs.answer: Keep the product’s pack count, size, servings and price explicit so it is distinguishable from a single unit.

faqs.question: Should every product have its INCI list?

faqs.question: How should shade ranges appear?
faqs.answer: Identify each shade as a distinct variant, with its correct name and manufacturer-assigned identifier where one exists.

faqs.question: Can a rewrite add “dermatologist tested”?

faqs.question: What if most sales come through retailers?
faqs.answer: Work on the sources you control. Retailers’ pages and claims remain under their control; ecentic does not change them automatically.

meta.description: Make model numbers, battery life, compatibility, connections and warranty clear. Compare electronics listings with named competitors.

consumer-electronics.title: Selling electronics when AI compares the spec sheet.
consumer-electronics.description: Electronics questions are often about battery life, compatibility or ports. Give each model and variant clear identifiers and source specifications so a comparison does not depend on a product name alone.
questions: noise-canceling earbuds with the longest battery under $200
Laptop for video editing with 32 GB of RAM
Robot vacuum that works with Google Home

faqs.question: Our model numbers differ by retailer. Does that matter?
faqs.answer: It can make matching ambiguous. Use the correct model and variant identifiers, and make any genuine retailer-specific configuration explicit.

faqs.question: Do we need GTINs?
faqs.answer: Provide the correct assigned GTIN where available. Never generate one or borrow it from a similar product.

faqs.question: Will a model compare on price alone?
faqs.answer: The question and available facts affect the comparison. State battery, compatibility and other relevant specifications so the model can inspect them.

faqs.question: How should refurbished products appear?
faqs.answer: State refurbished condition, the actual configuration, price and warranty terms. Do not present them as new.

home-and-furniture.name: Home and furniture

meta.title: Selling furniture and homeware through AI
meta.description: Make dimensions, materials, assembly, delivery and returns clear in furniture listings. Start with facts your team can verify.

home-and-furniture.title: Selling furniture when AI has to measure the room.
home-and-furniture.description: People describe their room, budget and practical needs. A useful comparison needs dimensions, materials and delivery terms in readable text. Keep exact product measurements separate from illustrative photos.
questions: Sofa bed that fits a 2-meter wall
Solid wood dining table for six under €1,000
Rug that is safe for underfloor heating

faqs.question: Our dimensions are only in a drawing. Is that a problem?
faqs.answer: Add the same verified dimensions as text with units. That provides explicit values tools can inspect without interpreting the drawing.

faqs.question: How should made-to-order lead times appear?
faqs.answer: State the actual production and delivery window and explain what can change. Do not present made-to-order stock as immediately available.

faqs.question: We offer one sofa in 20 fabrics. How should it look?
faqs.answer: Identify each variant’s fabric, color, price and availability. Use correct dimensions if a variant changes them.

faqs.question: Can AI buy a sofa for someone?
faqs.answer: It depends on the channel and supported checkout flow. Test delivery requirements and payment handoffs on a staging store before enabling agent orders.

sections.title: What your product data needs to say.

items.title: Dimensions
items.body: Width, depth and height with explicit units, plus packed size where available.

items.title: Materials
items.body: Frame, upholstery and finish described separately.

items.title: Capacity
items.body: Seats, tested weight limit or sleeping area from the supplier.

items.title: Assembly
items.body: Whether assembly is needed, supplied tools and instructions.

items.title: Delivery
items.body: Lead time, delivery to the room or door, and charges.

items.title: Returns
items.body: Return window, conditions and who pays collection costs.

sections.note: These are attributes for your team to verify, not fields ecentic automatically invents or enriches. The current feed importer supports a defined field mapping.

sections.title: Keep the rules with the product facts.
paragraphs: Article 19 of the EU General Product Safety Regulation requires online offers to show specified manufacturer or responsible-person information, product identification and relevant warnings. Check how it applies to the product you sell.
Keep special delivery terms explicit. A listing rewrite does not change shipping configuration or verify a load-bearing safety claim.
sections.note: Sources checked 10 November 2026. Requirements can depend on the product, channel and country.

fashion-and-outdoor.name: Fashion and outdoor

meta.title: Selling clothing and outdoor gear through AI
meta.description: Make sizing, materials, performance ratings and variants clear. Check textile and environmental claims before publishing listing changes.

fashion-and-outdoor.title: Selling clothing when AI has to get the size right.
fashion-and-outdoor.description: Shoppers ask for gear that fits a body, a climate and an activity. Give them size systems, fit notes and fabric facts that can be checked. Performance and environmental claims need evidence for the exact product.
questions: Waterproof jacket for hiking in Scotland
Running shoes for wide feet with good cushioning
Merino base layer that does not itch

faqs.question: Do we need the size chart in the feed?
faqs.answer: Submit supported size fields and variants. Keep verified fit notes and measurements available as readable text; a generic importer does not preserve every custom size-chart format.

faqs.question: How should 30 color and size variants appear?
faqs.answer: Each variant should carry the correct color, size, price and availability. Use its own identifier where one is assigned.

faqs.question: Can we call a product sustainable?
faqs.answer: Do not treat a generic environmental statement as harmless copy. Check the evidence and the rules applicable in the market; ecentic does not certify the claim.

faqs.question: Does this help on a marketplace with its own assistant?
faqs.answer: It lets you improve data sources you control. A marketplace controls its own listings, assistant and access rules.

paragraphs: Google’s size guidance requires size data for specified clothing and shoe listings, with requirements varying by destination and format. Check the exact apparel attributes for your market.

EU Directive 2024/825 calls for measures applying from 27 September 2026 that prohibit generic environmental claims without relevant recognized excellent environmental performance. Verify the national implementation before using a claim.

health-wellness-and-pet.name: Health, wellness and pet

meta.title: Selling wellness and pet products through AI
meta.description: Make ingredients, life stage, feeding guidance and supported claims explicit. Prepare wellness and pet product data within platform policies.

health-wellness-and-pet.title: Selling wellness and pet products when AI checks the facts.
health-wellness-and-pet.description: People ask what is in a product, who it is for and how to use it. Make ingredients and manufacturer instructions readable, and separate ordinary product information from medical or nutritional claims that need evidence.
questions: Grain-free food for a senior dog with a sensitive stomach
Magnesium supplement without fillers
Low-dust cat litter

faqs.question: Will you write health claims for us?
faqs.answer: We do not offer health-claim creation or validation. Listing work uses existing product facts; you must verify the statements allowed for your market.

faqs.question: Can a shopping assistant sell supplements?
faqs.answer: Eligibility depends on the platform, product and location. Some products are restricted or prohibited; a working checkout does not override those policies.

faqs.question: Our pet food has life-stage versions. How should it appear?
faqs.answer: Give each product its correct intended life stage, analysis and feeding guide. Do not transfer instructions from a different formulation.

faqs.question: Do you handle prescription products?
faqs.answer: Prescription products are outside the proposed marketing and pilot scope on this page.

items.title: Standards and testing
items.body: The nutritional adequacy statement where applicable and named third-party tests where supported.

items.title: Size and servings
items.body: Pack size and servings per pack, with clear units.

items.title: Product purpose
items.body: A supported description that stays within the rules of the market.

sections.note: These are attributes for your team to verify, not fields ecentic automatically invents or enriches. The current feed importer supports a defined field mapping.

sections.title: Keep the rules with the product facts.
paragraphs: Nutrition and health claims for human food supplements in the EU are subject to Regulation 1924/2006. A product description is not permission to make an unapproved health claim.
Google restricts or prohibits specified healthcare products and unapproved pharmaceuticals or supplements. Check the exact product category and target-country policy.
ecentic does not diagnose conditions, prescribe products or certify health claims. Keep rewritten information tied to verified source facts.
sections.note: Sources checked 10 November 2026. Requirements can depend on the product, channel and country.

travel-and-experiences.name: Travel and experiences

meta.title: Selling trips and experiences through AI
meta.description: Make dates, total prices, inclusions and cancellation terms readable. Explore a travel pilot that starts from public pages and product data.

travel-and-experiences.title: Selling trips when AI plans the holiday.
travel-and-experiences.description: People ask AI where to go, what to book and what it costs. Make dates, prices and terms clear on the pages you control. A travel pilot starts from your public site and agreed product data, without assuming a booking-engine integration.
questions: City break in Lisbon for a long weekend in May
Food tour in Mexico City for two
Ski chalet in the Alps for eight people

faqs.question: Can AI book a trip for someone?
faqs.answer: It depends on the channel and booking flow. This pilot does not promise an automated booking integration; we examine the public information and agreed handoff path.

faqs.question: Does this help direct bookings if we use booking sites too?
faqs.answer: It helps your team improve the information on pages you control. We do not guarantee that an assistant links to your site instead of a booking platform.

faqs.question: Do you need our booking engine?
faqs.answer: No for the public-data baseline. Later access or integration work needs a separately agreed scope.

faqs.question: Which markets do you cover?
faqs.answer: We start with one agreed market per pilot and confirm language and data coverage before beginning.
